prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create a single independent transparent cutout vignette for an established natural-history atlas website, wide 3:2 canvas. Refined museum natural-history plate: accurate natural forms, fine engraved ink detail and restrained watercolor washes, lifelike surface textures, elegant and tactile, same visual language as detailed botanical specimen illustrations. One complete small habitat scene centred with ample transparent margin and an irregular organic silhouette; all visible environment belongs to the vignette. No rectangular image frame, no solid or paper background, no floating geometric cube, no diagram, no UI, no text, no numbers, no measurements, no labels, no border, no people or equipment, no fantasy lighting. This is a conceptual habitat illustration, not a research result. Keep the silhouette legible when displayed about 400px wide on both warm off-white and charcoal. Real alpha transparency outside the scene.
Subject: a miniature patch of temperate mixed forest with five to seven trees of visibly different heights, layered irregular broadleaf crowns and two slender conifers, moss, fern understory and a tiny visible patch of earth. Slightly elevated oblique viewpoint so both canopy relief and tree trunks are readable. A broad mature tree on one side and shorter growth on the other, not a line of equal-height trees. Deep olive, soft pine green, warm bark and muted ochre, subtle depth. Entire trees visible, richly observed foliage. The varying canopy height is the main visual idea.
